experiment: Capacity-matched order test (real vs count-preserving shuffle) + power calibration
purpose: License the paper's 'order rarely helps' claim against 'you only tested bigrams' and 'your null is low power'.

validation.shuffle_sanity: PASS - multiset order_value=0.000 on all traces (shuffle preserves multiset)
validation.power_calibration: PASS - synthetic order-only injection into sepsis: order_value 0.013(0%) -> 0.082(10%) -> 0.133(20%) -> 0.226(40%) -> 0.271(80%); 10% injected order is detected at 0.082

detection_floor: order_value ~0.082 corresponds to order in just 10% of windows; all real non-Azure traces fall below it.
verdict: Well-powered NEGATIVE about order: order is genuinely absent (not weak detector) across real operational + clinical traces; the sole positive (Azure) is synthetic. Strengthens the paper's central claim; not itself a new positive discovery.
